rows.title: Macroeconomic uncertainties will not halt progress on the energy transition in 2024 and beyond. Here’s why
rows.standfirst: Cost inflation and high interest rates have affected renewables–but policymakers are already responding and new auction mechanisms are being put in place.

rows.title: 2023 was a dud for New York City real estate—‘even for rich people.’ This year isn’t shaping up to be much better, Coldwell Banker office says
rows.standfirst: Both the rental and residential real estate markets were slow in 2023.

rows.title: Iceland’s booming tourist industry and hot housing market is leaving locals out in the cold
rows.standfirst: Increased tourism, which accounts for about 6% of Iceland’s GDP, has meant a greater demand for workers and therefore a greater need for housing.

rows.title: Zillow’s chief economist published a New Year’s ‘Housing Market Resolutions’ list. It reveals just how dire things have gotten
rows.standfirst: From the lock-in effect, to the housing shortage, to mortgage rates and more—here’s what Zillow’s chief economist is wishing for in this year’s housing market.

rows.title: The dean of NYC’s housing market dissects a puzzle: Manhattan’s record-high number of all-cash home sales. He sees good news ahead on mortgage rates
rows.standfirst: Master appraiser Jonathan Miller has been tracking the value of Manhattan real estate every week for 40 years, and he’s never seen it quite like this before.

rows.title: Shipping giant Maersk’s stock buoyed by halt of Red Sea journeys following Houthi rebel attacks—but it may be bad news for inflation
rows.standfirst: Global shipping leaders and oil giant BP have decided to hit pause on Red Sea transit until it becomes safer—but costs could increase as a result.

rows.title: There’s a flicker of life in the housing market as average mortgage payments plummet nearly $400 over 2 months and buyers start to stir again, Redfin says
rows.standfirst: The median mortgage payment fell 14% to $2,361 in December from a record high in October, when mortgage rates hit a 23-year peak.

rows.title: A supermarket chain has gone beyond shaming PepsiCo for ‘shrinkflation’—now it’s pulling Cheetos and Doritos off the shelves across Europe
rows.standfirst: PepsiCo’s price increases are simply “unacceptable,” according to French supermarket giant Carrefour. The government agrees.

rows.title: Commercial real estate has a ‘muted’ outlook after a near-death experience in 2023, Moody’s economist says—and ‘office will continue to face the most strain’
rows.standfirst: “Across all sectors,” says Ermengarde Jabir, senior economist with Moody’s Analytics, “there will be a continued recalibration of sorts.”

rows.title: Paris hotels are cashing in on Olympics fever by hiking prices to over $1,000 on opening night
rows.standfirst: Paris hotels are gearing up for a buzzy summer as the Olympics, expected to receive 15 million visitors, nears.

rows.title: Despite Europe’s economic woes, consumers are sticking to their guns on sustainability
rows.standfirst: While budgets were still tight for many European families this year, shoppers’ commitment to sustainability remains firm.

rows.title: Biden’s economic guru insists both Wall Street and Main Street can celebrate another strong jobs report as the market yawns
rows.standfirst: “At the end of the day, this idea that what’s good for Main Street is bad for Wall Street is not really correct,” Jared Bernstein, chair of the Council of Economic Advisers, told Fortune.

rows.title: Rent is so expensive for Gen Zers that almost one-third are living with their parents, new report finds
rows.standfirst: Affordable housing is a thing of the past for Gen Z.

rows.title: ‘What planet does he live on?’ Bank boss sparks fury after saying it’s ‘not that difficult’ to buy a home in cost-of-living crisis-hit U.K.
rows.standfirst: Critics called NatWest chair Davies’s comment a “staggering demonstration of the disconnect between bankers and reality in this country.”

rows.title: A supermarket chain pulled PepsiCo products over ‘shrinkflation’—now its biggest rival says Pepsi, Cheetos and Doritos are going nowhere
rows.standfirst: E.Leclerc’s chairman said he wouldn’t follow Carrefour’s “show of strength” by banning Cheetos and Doritos from his stores.

rows.title: The brutal 2023 housing market was just like the 1980s—except with a little bit of Global Financial Crisis thrown in
rows.standfirst: Millennials face a housing market a lot like their parents experienced—with a dash of their early adulthood added, for good measure.

rows.title: Wharton’s Jeremy Siegel says the U.S. economy is at a perfect ‘Goldilocks pace’—neither too strong nor too weak to spook the Fed or markets
rows.standfirst: “Everyone is focused on how many rate cuts are priced [in] … and how we need six cuts to have a good 2024. I totally disagree with that.”

rows.title: Optimism among CFOs about economic conditions declines, but they remain confident in harnessing tech for long-term gains
rows.standfirst: Interest rates, the macroeconomic economy, and geopolitics are CFOs’ top three concerns, according to Deloitte’s new analysis.

rows.title: Detroit dethroned Miami as fastest-appreciating housing market as home prices continued their climb in late 2023, CoreLogic says
rows.standfirst: U.S. home prices were up 5.2% in November 2023, the strongest annual growth rate since January of last year.

rows.title: PepsiCo and a French supermarket giant are arguing over who dumped who first in ‘shrinkflation’ tussle
rows.standfirst: Both PepsiCo and Carrefour are now taking credit for removing PepsiCo products from the supermarket’s shelves.

rows.title: The housing market is heading for the affordability of 2 years ago, Morgan Stanley says. Here’s why its home price forecast is unchanged
rows.standfirst: “Home prices have once again broken through to a new record high,” James Egan says, but the bank still sees them dropping in 2024.

rows.title: Kathy Hochul unveils huge $500 million housing plan to fix New York state crisis, but she’s avoiding the suburbs
rows.standfirst: Senate Democrats, meanwhile, are pushing for a housing agreement that focuses on tenant protections—not building more housing.

rows.title: Americans across racial backgrounds list the economy as the top issue in 2024—but disagree about most everything else—according to major new polls
rows.standfirst: Immigration was named as a top priority for government action by 43% of Hispanic adults, 36% of white adults and 29% of Asians and Pacific Islanders, but only 19% of Black adults.

rows.title: Danone will cut baby formula prices by 7% after U.K. antitrust watchdog probe into prices that rose 25% in 2 years
rows.standfirst: Baby formula prices have risen by 25% over the last two years. 85% of the baby formula is dominated by two companies, and Danone has a market share of around 70%.

rows.title: With Trump’s tax cuts expiring, taxes could increase for most Americans after next year. Here’s how to plan ahead
rows.standfirst: “Planning early is important.”

rows.title: The economy just handed boomers another win—the U.S. housing market nearly doubled in a decade to a record $23 trillion
rows.standfirst: U.S. homeowners with mortgages were sitting on $23 trillion in housing wealth by the end of 2022.

rows.title: Jennifer Garner-Hamdi Ulukaya: ‘1 in 5 American kids may go to bed hungry tonight–and unprecedented attacks on the 50-year-old bipartisan WIC program could make the situation even worse’
rows.standfirst: ‘Our country has never turned its back on hungry children. But unless Congress acts to provide full funding by Jan. 19, we will have done just that.’

rows.title: Inflation hotter than expected in December, signaling bumpy ride ahead in supposed soft landing for the economy
rows.standfirst: Overall prices rose 0.3% from November and 3.4% from 12 months earlier, compared to respective increases of 0.1% and 3.1% the previous month.

rows.title: Luxury trench-coat maker Burberry is buttoning up for a gloomy earnings report after Christmas washout
rows.standfirst: “Unlike your average fashion retailer, it is simply not the Burberry way to slash prices and hope bargains lure in shoppers,” AJ Bell’s Russ Mould said.

rows.title: Wholesale prices in December went in reverse even as consumer inflation heated up
rows.standfirst: Producer prices fell for the third month in a row in December, declining 0.1% and rising a mild 1% on an annual basis.

rows.title: Europe’s largest economy, struggling to pull itself out of recession, hit with rail strikes and farmers’ protests to start 2024
rows.standfirst: Chancellor Olaf Scholz is slipping in polls, while a surging far-right party is backing the protesting farmers, who are losing some of their precious subsidies.

rows.title: Those falling mortgage rates don’t mean falling home prices, Capital Economics says, revising its forecast up for the year
rows.standfirst: The research firm’s property economist, Thomas Ryan, called its house price forecast “well above the consensus,” in a new research note.

rows.title: Ruptured supply chains, rising oil prices, and resurgent inflation. The Red Sea crisis is rekindling memories of the Ukraine War—but this time could be different
rows.standfirst: When it comes to longer term economic impacts of the Red Sea crisis: The “most honest answer” experts can give is “I have no idea” at this point, Unlimited’s Bob Elliott told Fortune.

rows.title: Don’t expect interest rate cuts anytime soon, says former Fed bank examiner
rows.standfirst: This will have an impact on the big U.S. banks, according to Mark T. Williams.

rows.title: Swiss chocolate maker Lindt’s record sales growth comes with a bitter twist—the customer swallowed much of the added costs
rows.standfirst: The maker of Lindor pralines said it was able to pass cocoa costs onto customers as it expects to increase profits.

rows.title: Boomers’ dominance of the housing market is so complete that empty nesters own twice as many large homes as millennials with kids, Redfin analysis reveals
rows.standfirst: “The landscape has transformed over the last decade: 10 years ago, young families were just as likely as empty nesters to own large homes.”

rows.title: 3 reasons why the frozen housing market of 2024 is actually more competitive than before the pandemic, Zillow says
rows.standfirst: It’s all about the (lack of) inventory.

rows.title: Treasury Secretary Yellen pushes back against Republican criticism—U.S. economic growth ‘vindicates’ Biden’s pandemic stimulus spending
rows.standfirst: As President Joe Biden seeks reelection, he is trying to convince voters who are gloomy about the economy that inflation is under control and the economy is strong.

rows.title: Inflation, employment picture ‘almost as good as it gets,’ top Federal Reserve official says
rows.standfirst: Christopher Waller wrote to the Brookings Institution that he is “feeling more confident that the economy can continue along its current trajectory.”

rows.title: Deutsche Bank’s finance chief says we’re living through a ‘pinch me moment’
rows.standfirst: Chief financial officer James von Moltke says the economy is surviving against all odds despite inflation, rate hikes, and wars.

rows.title: One chart shows how it’s boomers’ housing market, we’re all just living in it—but Gen Z just might have a good head start
rows.standfirst: “Housing affordability remains strained, but things are looking up for Gen Z,” said Redfin’s chief economist, Daryl Fairweather.

rows.title: Coca-Cola’s CEO isn’t making the same mistake as rival PepsiCo—he’s prioritizing ‘long-term security’ over spats with supermarkets
rows.standfirst: “We don’t go up very quickly and we don’t tend to crash back down, we like the idea of seeing the cycle through.”

rows.title: Did the housing market just hit a bottom? New data reveals home sales hit their lowest point in 28 years in 2023
rows.standfirst: Some experts see a thaw as mortgage rates look set to fall. But on the other hand, “the recent, rapid three-year rise in home prices is unsustainable.”

rows.title: The vibecession is in recession as cooling inflation and rising wages have Americans feeling better about the economy in the new year
rows.standfirst: “The vibes are catching up with the hard data on the economy,” said Arindrajit Dube, provost professor of economics at UMass Amherst.

rows.title: Soaring insurance rates are making it more expensive than ever to own a car, and the entire auto industry is feeling the pain
rows.standfirst: After years of low growth, insurance saw double-digit rate increases for two years running.

rows.title: Wall Street’s landlord phase is back on, as Blackstone’s $3.8 billion acquisition of Tricon rouses a slumbering institutional investing sector
rows.standfirst: Tricon owns 7,000 units in Atlanta and other major markets include Charlotte, North Carolina; Tampa, Florida; Dallas, Phoenix, and Houston.

rows.title: Wall Street celebrates record highs for stocks as 2 of the 3 major indexes hit new peaks, and some analysts see room to run
rows.standfirst: The S&P 500 rose to a record high of 4,839 on Friday, while the Dow keeps setting new records itself.

rows.title: ‘Greedflation’ caused more than half of last year’s inflation surge, study finds, as corporate profits remain at all-time highs
rows.standfirst: Groundwork Collaborative crunched Commerce Department data to find shocking greedflation results. But there’s evidence of it in a lot more places.

rows.title: The least affordable housing market in more than a generation is facing another threat: Uninsurable properties
rows.standfirst: “Your home is generally your biggest asset,” says CoreLogic’s Garret Gray. “If you can’t insure your safe space, think of the emotional toll of that.”

rows.title: 5 Gen Xers share what it’s really like to plan for retirement: ‘My generation is going to have a harder time than boomers’
rows.standfirst: The oldest Gen Xers are approaching retirement. Are they ready?

rows.title: ‘Greedflation’ is a problem for central banks now, with Richmond Fed’s Barkin worried that corporate price hikes are baked into the system
rows.standfirst: After companies got a taste of “greedflation” in the pandemic, bringing prices down will be a doozy, predicts Tom Barkin.

rows.title: Top markets analyst sees 3 scenarios for stocks in the 2020s, and only one of them is a bad outcome
rows.standfirst: Stagflation, the Roaring’20s, or another ’90s-style tech bubble? Ed Yardeni called last year’s market rally and he says we are at a fork in the road.

rows.title: Hawaii governor struggles with tourist-driven housing market: ‘I don’t want to be rude, but I do want people to realize that that market should be for our local families’
rows.standfirst: Gov. Josh Green has been unable to permanently resettle 5,000 families displaced by August’s wildfire in Maui.

rows.title: Compass CEO says housing market is poised for a rebound after 2023’s ‘modest buyer strike’ caused 39% of all listed home prices to drop
rows.standfirst: “All the key signs are pointing in the right direction,” said Robert Reffkin, whose brokerage’s stock is down over 80% since going public amid the boom of 2021.

rows.title: Slower inflation, higher incomes, lower gas prices and a rising stock market—Americans are starting to like the economy
rows.standfirst: A measure of consumer sentiment by the University of Michigan has jumped in the past two months by the most since 1991.

rows.title: Ikea is busy cutting prices while everything else gets expensive—and the group’s CEO says it wasn’t ‘rocket science’ to make that call
rows.standfirst: “Right now, we’re lowering prices more than we’ve ever done,” Jesper Brodin, CEO of Ikea’s parent company, Ingka Group, said.

rows.title: The housing market is in its worst slump since 1995. NAR says the ‘world was much different’ then—here’s how
rows.standfirst: “2023 may well have the unique distinction of being incomparable and, hopefully, quickly a distant memory,” says First American’s Mark Fleming.

rows.title: A crippled housing market has left Americans stranded in 40-year-old properties and unable to afford most home improvements. Now they are turning to ‘home hardening’ instead
rows.standfirst: 38% of homes in the U.S. were built before 1970–and the median age of homes in America is 40 years.

rows.title: Legendary LBO billionaire David Rubenstein sees opportunity in multifamily housing and industrial properties, raising $400 million fund, sources say
rows.standfirst: Declaration Partners is seeking to raise about $400 million from wealthy individuals and family offices, said people with knowledge of the matter.

rows.title: Harvard economist Jason Furman says the soft landing is here—and the risk we ‘veer off the runway’ into recession is not ‘unusually high’
rows.standfirst: From inevitable recession to “sustained growth,” the U.S. economy continues to surprise economists.

rows.title: Zillow just raised its home price forecast, seeing a 3.7% jump in 2024, and it’s all because of ‘external factors’
rows.standfirst: Zillow economist Nicole Bachaud said increased affordability “unlocks some more buyers to be able to shop for a home if rates stay lower this spring.”

rows.title: The Fed’s preferred inflation metric cooled again in December as soft landing beckons
rows.standfirst: The core Personal Consumption Expenditures index rose 0.2% from November while cooling to 2.9% year-over-year—both lower than expected.

rows.title: 28-year-old first-time homebuyer says ‘it’s a little bit of a crash course’ going from having roommates to being a landlord
rows.standfirst: “I walked into this house that I wound up buying, and within five minutes, I was like, I have to put an offer on it,” Leif Jonasson told Fortune.

rows.title: ‘This Old House’ just took a look at the American Dream of homeownership, and sees ‘evident desperation’ among homebuyers
rows.standfirst: “2023 was a wash” for many potential homebuyers, This Old House says after surveying 3,000 for its Aspiring Homeowners report.

rows.title: How tiny homes went from a millennial lifestyle fad to a Hail Mary shot at solving the homeless crisis
rows.standfirst: The mini versions of detached single-family homes are an extension of Americans’ obsession with a development style that’s partly responsible for the current crisis.

rows.title: Amid U.S. construction boom, world’s largest cement maker will spin off North American business, seek $30B valuation: ‘Two independent champions’
rows.standfirst: Holcim sees U.S. builders racing to relieve a lack of single-family homes and meet regulatory pressures for more energy-efficient buildings.

rows.title: ‘Buying a home is not even remotely possible‘ for many Americans, says Moody’s chief economist
rows.standfirst: “Death, divorce, children, or job change” aren’t budging homeowners locked into low rates, Mark Zandi says.

rows.title: Elizabeth Warren is furious about the ‘full-blown housing crisis’ and she’s targeting Jerome Powell’s ‘troubling rate hikes’
rows.standfirst: “We urge you to consider the effects of your interest rate decisions on the housing market,” Warren and colleagues wrote to the central bank.

rows.title: You have to be ‘wealthy or lucky’ to buy a home in this housing market, says top economist Ali Wolf
rows.standfirst: “In the past, if you were middle class, it was almost assumed you would become a homeowner. Today, the aspiration is still there, but it is a lot more difficult.”

rows.title: ‘Black Swan’ author Nassim Taleb, who correctly called the 2008 financial crisis, says the U.S. is in a ‘death spiral’ over government debt
rows.standfirst: “We need something to come in from the outside, or maybe some kind of miracle.”

rows.title: Taylor Swift is nearly as big a deal (economically) to your city as hosting the Super Bowl, BofA says
rows.standfirst: The bank calculates a $77 boost to restaurants and $56 to bars the night of the Eras Tour, versus $96 and $74 for the big game.

rows.title: The markets are starting to realize just how hawkish the Fed is–and reckoning with higher-for-longer interest rates
rows.standfirst: Sticky core inflation and new hawkish FOMC members could delay any interest rate cuts.

frame: Union of four fixed economic tags
